## Problem

`decideDailyRelease` (`daily-release.ts`, v2026.11.14 / 7687a35) resumes any untagged `package.json` version as `pending`:

```ts
const pending = current && /^\d{4}\.\d{1,2}\.\d{1,2}(-\d+)?$/.test(current)
  && !input.releaseTags.some(tag => releaseCoordinate(tag) === releaseCoordinate(current)) ? current : undefined;
const version = input.packageVersion ?? pending ?? releaseVersion(input.today);
```

That rule lets a release that merged but was never tagged resume after a day rollover. Packages whose first npm version was published by hand (no git tag, no provenance) also look exactly like that. prepare then builds a candidate for a version npm already holds, the release PR merges, and the release step must refuse it:

> `<pkg>@<version> exists on the registry without matching commit and artifact provenance ... Refusing to tag and release around it`

The next prepare picks the same untagged version again, so these packages can never release through the flow.

## Evidence (2026-11-16)

| Package | package.json / candidate on main | npm latest | git tags |
|---|---|---|---|
| pm-review | 2026.10.12 (release PR #90 merged 16:45Z) | 2026.10.12 | 0 |
| pm-brand | 2026.10.17 (#53 merged 16:34Z) | 2026.10.17 | 0 |
| pm-rlm | 2026.10.18 | 2026.10.18 | 0 |
| pm-glossary | 2026.11.5 (#24 merged 17:05Z) | 2026.11.5 | 0 |
| pm-reduce, pm-screen | 2026.11.6 | 2026.11.6 | 0 |
| pm-unit, pm-hypothesis, pm-http | untagged = npm latest (next in line) | same | 0 |

The 11-15 pm-review and pm-rlm prepares also targeted 2026.10.12 and 2026.10.18.

## Proposal

- In prepare's `decide` step, before treating an untagged version as `pending`, check the registry (`npm view <name>@<version> dist --json`). If that version exists, it is not a resumable release, so fall through to `releaseVersion(today)`. Unit-test `decideDailyRelease` with a new `registryHasCurrentVersion` input for both cases.
- In reconcile/release, when the merged candidate's version already exists on npm without this flow's provenance, retire the candidate (the same path as `retire-unpublished`) and let the next prepare cut today's version. Today's behaviour, a red run on every reconcile, recovers nothing.
- Optional: record the hand-published first version as a GitHub release or tag without re-publishing, so the changelog and release list line up with npm.

## Acceptance

- A repository whose untagged `package.json` version already exists on npm gets a candidate for today's date, not the old version.
- A truly pending (merged, untagged, not yet on npm) version still resumes after a rollover.
- An already-merged stale candidate is retired with a clear notice instead of failing every hourly reconcile.
